A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PKU-SafeRLHF research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–D support reliable comparison despite formatting changes and relocated material.

before.justification: v2 reports original moderation and RLHF experiments in Tables 1–3, human–model evaluation analyses in Figure 6, and annotation-agreement results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains original moderation and RLHF results in Tables 1–3, human–model evaluation analyses in Figure 7, and annotation-agreement results in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The generation and annotation pipeline, severity-sensitive moderation, reward/cost models, and PPO/PPO-Lagrange procedures remain unchanged. New Appendix C.2 largely explains the GPT-4 assistance and human quality checks already documented in v2.

E1.justification: Both versions retain Alpaca 52K, PKU-SafeRLHF, and BeaverTails, with the same helpfulness, harmlessness, harm-category, and severity tasks. The added discussion of specialized domains and non-English contexts describes limitations rather than additional evaluations.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Llama-Guard, Llama-Guard 2, Perspective API, and OpenAI Moderation API. WildGuard is newly cited but not evaluated. Tables 2–3 retain the BeaverTails and single-/dual-preference comparisons; Table 3's shortened headers do not establish different comparators.

E3.justification: The retained experiments report the same metrics, model setups, annotation controls, and generation/training settings. Tables 5 and 9 preserve their parameters, including two training epochs and 20K examples. No revised testing protocol is documented.

E4.justification: The harm-category correlation and UMAP analyses, preference-decoupling comparison, human–model agreement/calibration analyses, and annotation cases remain. Section 3.4 reuses the existing prompt-distribution analysis. The deleted cross-model score overview is benchmark reporting rather than an ablation or robustness test.

E5.justification: Table 9 retains seed 42, and v2 Figure 6(b)/v3 Figure 7(b) retain the smoothed ±1 standard-deviation reporting. No new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures appear.

E6.justification: v2 Figure 6(c)'s helpfulness/harmlessness scores across named LLM families and its associated model-size/version findings are removed. The central moderation and RLHF results in Tables 1–3 match exactly, including 0.93 moderation accuracy and the 94.0% Alpaca2 dual-preference harmlessness win rate. Retained appendix results also match.

T1.justification: The Bradley–Terry preference formulation, harmfulness sign definition, reward/cost losses, and Appendix D PPO/PPO-Lagrange objectives are mathematically unchanged. Equation formatting and numbering change, without new assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same dataset contributions and claims concerning severity-sensitive moderation and single-/dual-preference safety alignment. Removing the cross-model score overview changes supporting results rather than the central contribution claims.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds specific limitations concerning legal, medical, and financial domains, English-language coverage, and cultural differences. Appendix C.2 explains why model refusals make human quality control necessary. Section 3.4 expands the interpretation of prompt diversity, while the discussion accompanying the deleted cross-model scores disappears.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 reattributes its quality-control account from BeaverTails to PKU-SafeRLHF. Removing Figure 6(c) also removes specific evaluation-model identifiers, including dated GPT-4 variants. Generation prompts, hardware, hyperparameters, annotation thresholds, and dataset access/license information otherwise remain; new C.2 largely repeats existing procedural details.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including WildGuard, Align Anything, Safe RLHF-V, deceptive-alignment mitigation, and generative reward-modeling work. Section 3.4 makes the comparison with BeaverTails more explicit, and the Gemma reference disappears with the score overview. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited wording edits, updates the author block and citation style, renames Section 4.2, and removes the duplicated opening of the conclusion. It adds Sections 3.4 and C.2 and separates limitations and ethical-labor discussion into Sections 6 and 7, while retaining most prose and the overall narrative.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from one column to two, with widespread resizing and repositioning of displays. The prompt-distribution figure moves into the main text, the evaluation figure loses panel (c), and Table 3 becomes compact with less explicit comparator headers. Appendix Tables 7–9 move to the final pages, substantially changing their placement relative to the discussion.

improvement.justification: v3 improves qualification through its domain, linguistic, and cultural limitations and its explanation of human quality control. However, it removes the cross-model comparative evidence in v2 Figure 6(c) and makes Table 3's comparator labels less clear. With the central methods and validation unchanged, these gains in explanation and losses in evidence and readability do not establish a reliable net quality direction.
